To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the transcription factor ETS is activated in diabetes.
the transcriptional activation of endothelial transcription factors is increased in diabetes.
diabetes leads to increased activation of ETS1 and that ETS1 downregulation rescues the reduction of endothelial progenitor cells in vitro and in mice.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms that are involved in the reduction of Vascular progenitor cells in type 2 diabetes.
the molecular basis for the impaired neovascularization in patients with type 1 and type 2 diabetes.
the molecular mechanism of impaired VPC number and function in diabetes and provides a potential therapeutic approach.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the transcription factors of the ETS family are involved in the pathophysiology of diabetes mellitus and the development of cardiovascular diseases.
diabetes leads to an impaired activation of ETS and that the inhibition of ETS restores functional activity of progenitors cells in vitro and in a mouse model.
diabetes-induced reduction of VPC is caused by the activation of the ETS transcription factor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the inhibition of p38 kinase and ETS1 is a promising therapeutic approach to increase VPC number and functional activity in patients with diabetes mellitus.
ETS1 is an important mediator in diabetes-induced impairment of progenitor cells.
ETS is a key transcription factor that mediates the negative effects of diabetes on VPC.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ETS is a critical regulator of progenitor cell function and that its dysregulation is a key event during diabetes-associated vascular dysfunction.
diabetes leads to a dysregulated activation of the transcription factors ETS1/2, which blocks the function and the commitment of VPC towards endothelial cell lineage.
ETS is a novel regulator of the functional activity and endothelial differentiation of progenitor cells.
